question: What did the United States and China agree in their 2025 trade truce?
text:
The 2025 truce came in three stages.

**1. Geneva, May 2025.** The two sides agreed that Trump's 20% fentanyl-related tariff would stay in place. Most of the broader trade-war measures were relaxed temporarily, for 90 days, through August 12, 2025.[1]

**2. August 2025 extension.** On August 11, Trump signed an executive order extending the truce by another 90 days, to November 10, 2025.[2] That stopped US tariffs from rising to 145% and Chinese tariffs from rising to 125%. Tariffs stayed at 30% on Chinese imports to the US and 10% on US exports to China.[3]

**3. Busan deal, October 30, 2025.** After Trump and Xi met in South Korea, the main terms were:

- **US tariffs:** The US cut the fentanyl-related tariff from 20% to 10%, which lowered the overall tariff rate on Chinese imports from 41% to 31%.[4]
- **US export controls and trade measures:**
  - The US suspended for one year, from November 10, 2025, its rule extending export controls to affiliates of listed entities.[5]
  - It also suspended for one year its actions under the Section 301 investigation into China's maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors.[5]
  - Certain Section 301 tariff exclusions were extended to November 10, 2026.[5]
- **Rare earths:** China will suspend for one year its October 2025 export controls on rare earth materials.[6] The status of its earlier April 2025 controls remains ambiguous.
- **Agriculture:** China will buy at least 12 million metric tons of US soybeans in the last two months of 2025.[5] It also committed to buying at least 25 million metric tons in later years. China pledged to resume imports of soybeans and other US agricultural products.[7]
- **Countermeasures:** China will suspend or remove the non-tariff countermeasures it has taken against the US since March 4, 2025. These include listing certain American companies on its end-user and unreliable-entity lists.[5] The White House fact sheet also says China will end its investigations targeting US companies.
- **Fentanyl:** The two sides agreed to strengthen cooperation against fentanyl.[7]

Analysts called it limited. One law-firm summary described it as "a limited but meaningful thaw"[6], and major disputes remain, particularly over semiconductors and rare earths.[4]

More recently, Treasury Secretary Bessent said the two countries agreed to extend what he called the "Busan Agreement"[8] to January 10. That gives them more time to decide whether to pursue a broader deal.
